releaseNotes: Product differentiation becomes doctrine with an enforced wedge artifact. The 2026-07-26 audit's sixth commercial gap: the skill carried no product-moat thinking, so launches shipped commodity apps into categories owned by incumbents and the 11-star process polished an undifferentiated core. references/product-moat.md is the new doctrine — name the incumbent, state the wedge the incumbent structurally cannot copy in a week, and classify the moat (data, workflow, community, taste, model, or distribution) — and templates/SPEC.md gains a Differentiation And Moat section holding the incumbent table, the moat-class line, and the one-week-copy test answer. check:product-spec enforces the section at done: at least one real incumbent row beyond the example (position-parsed header, five filled cells), a moat class naming one of the six classes, and a non-empty one-week-copy answer (product_spec.incumbent_row_missing / moat_class_missing / copy_test_missing). The four archetype positioning prompts instruct transcribing the moat conclusions into SPEC.md, artifact-contracts.md records the SPEC contract, the 11-star router row loads the doctrine, and LaunchBench scenario commodity-wedge-never-challenged.yaml teaches the failure. Fixtures pin the real-row positive and both missing-element negatives. Review hardening: an absent or prose-mentioned section runs the same substance checks against nothing (all three errors fire instead of a silent skip), and the one-week-copy answer must be substantive — placeholder vocabulary is rejected. Two more fixtures. Second round: a conceding copy-test answer (nothing stops them) is a failed test, a negated class declaration cannot pass by naming the taxonomy it disclaims (the doctrine's V1 no-moat exception is honored only with a named class and real date), and N/A/none/unknown cells name no incumbent. Four more fixtures. Third round: the moat-class parse anchors to the labeled field so the template's own guidance prose cannot shadow the answer (the filled shipped template now passes, pinned), the doctrine's named nonanswers (better designed, not thought of it) fail the copy test, negated structural answers (cannot be copied in a week) survive via polarity-aware concession tests, and the V1 exception requires its day-30 revisit alongside the named class and date. Five more fixtures. Fourth round: taxonomy polarity is clause-level in both directions (data is not a moat fails), can-ship-in-a-week concessions fail without the word copy, and the V1 revisit binds to day 30 — an annual retro is the moat-someday state wearing a commitment. Three more fixtures. Fifth round: the class must arrive with its build plan (a bare taxonomy word fails), and the V1 exception requires an affirmative build commitment — refusing to build the named class captures the same words and fails. Two more fixtures. Sixth round: the build plan needs a negation-free clause of real text (a plan refusing the moat it names fails), negative contractions void the V1 commitment, and copy-test negation is scoped to the predicate it negates so an unrelated 'not' cannot erase a live shipping concession. Three more fixtures. Seventh round: the incumbent table needs at least two real rows (§3 benchmarks the top 2-3 — one row compares against a category of one), the declared class is parsed from the head clause so taxonomy words inside the plan cannot bless an invalid class like execution, and leading-negation structural answers (No incumbent can reproduce…) are claims, not concessions. Three more fixtures.

check:source-registry no longer scans machine-local .claude/worktrees/* checkouts. Those directories are concurrent agent worktrees of other branches living inside the primary checkout, so a sibling agent's in-progress file carrying a not-yet-registered URL turned the maintainer's local audit red while CI (clean clone, no nested worktrees) stayed green — the URL belongs to that branch's own audit, which registers it before merge. Same exclusion class as the npm-pack .claude rule and the generated source-refresh.html report. The exclusion compares path segments rather than a separator-literal prefix, so it holds on Windows path separators too (Codex review catch).

A validator fixture (source-registry-worktree-copy) pins the worktree exclusion: a clean registry plus a nested .claude/worktrees copy holding an unregistered URL must pass, using the same assembled-URL construction as the generated-artifact pin so the fixture file itself stays invisible to the repo-level scan.

Every growth and money playbook now has a scale phase. The 2026-07-26 audit found the skill specified Day-0 discovery in detail and left the scaled state undefined everywhere that matters past the first win: the paywall shipped once and was never touched (anti-pattern #10 diagnosed the failure, nothing enforced the cure), UGC stopped at a 3-5 creator roster with 'scaling' appearing only as a warning, push notifications had one event name while email had a 318-line reference, and the viral lane counted shares without ever computing whether the loop compounds.

Paywall experimentation becomes a standing program: revenue-monetization.md §7b (the first paywall is a hypothesis — timing, packaging, trial shape, price, offer, design last; one experiment per surface, judged on cohort economics over a renewal-decision window; RevenueCat Experiments when available), REVENUE_OPS.md's Paywall Experiment Backlog table, and check:revenue requiring a dated active or completed non-placeholder row once the app has been live four weeks with the revenue lane done (revenue.experiment_backlog.missing/.empty, live_since validated with the same strict round-trip as the post-launch clock) — a backlog of empty headers is the one-and-done plateau wearing a green check.

Push becomes a lifecycle discipline: references/push-notification-lifecycle.md is the email system's sibling (provider setup, the primed permission ask placed after the first value moment and never beside the review popup, a segmented six-trigger table, server-enforced frequency caps with quiet hours, and the ethics line — every trigger serves the user's stated goal, guilt copy banned). The six push events join the ANALYTICS.md catalog, onboarding-conversion.md carries the priming placement, and the Email + push routing row loads the reference. UGC gains the Post-Breakout Scale Model (3-5 → 10 → 30 → 75+ creator bands with weekly volume, budget-per-band founder gates, and fatigue measured by install-per-video decay), viral-growth-loops.md gains Loop Economics (k = invites per active × recipient conversion, cycle time, honest k bands, a worked example) with VIRAL_GROWTH.md's weekly k table enforced by check:viral-growth (viral_growth.loop_economics.missing), and two LaunchBench scenarios (paywall-experimentation-never-starts, push-lifecycle-never-built) plus three fixtures pin the additions. Review round made every scale contract enforceable: check:viral-growth requires a measured Loop Economics region at done (k = <value>, a dated measured row, or a dated first-measurement commitment — the heading alone is counting shares with extra steps) and fails a UGC playbook that stops at the Day-0 roster (viral_growth.ugc_scale_model_missing, with the Post-Breakout Scale Model table now shipped in the template); check:onboarding fails a done contract with no push permission prime and no recorded not-applicable decision (onboarding.push_priming_missing, the template carries the prime row, and the push LaunchBench scenario cites this validator); and check:revenue parses the backlog's Status and Started cells by header column so 'completed' inside a hypothesis satisfies nothing and a legitimate active row with a pending result still counts. Four more fixtures. Second round: the disable event keeps its canonical name (notification_disabled, matching the emotional-design contract and Dark-Pattern Watch counter-metric — no split funnel); the push gate validates placement, not mention (the prime line must sit at an earned post-value moment and a cold ask on launch is itself the error); the UGC scale check requires the substantive model (three-plus named bands, founder-gated budgets, install-per-video/fatigue — keyword confetti fails); and the backlog's Started date round-trips as a real past calendar date like every other clock in the suite. Three more fixtures. Third round: a done growth lane with no UGC playbook fails (viral_growth.ugc_playbook_missing — a deleted playbook is the Day-0 ceiling with the evidence removed; creator content recorded as out of scope in VIRAL_GROWTH.md is the one escape), the loop-economics region is delimited at the next section boundary so dated numbers in Traceability cannot read as measurements, and push placement requires the after/earned anchoring — naming the value-reveal while asking before it is itself the violation. Three more fixtures. Fourth round: negated guidance ('never on launch') documents the prohibition and no longer false-fires the cold-ask scan, the loop-economics region anchors to the real section heading so a table-of-contents mention cannot orphan the measured section, and docs/VALIDATORS.md's check:onboarding/check:revenue/check:viral-growth rows name the new gates. Two more fixtures. Fifth round converged the parse rigor: aspirational k targets are not measurements (target/goal language on the k line disqualifies it), loop-measurement dates round-trip with due dates bounded to 60 days out, UGC bands count only with roster numbers beside them and founder-gated/budget language (bare labels and bare 'founder' satisfy nothing), and push-clause polarity is evaluated per clause so a negated placement with an affirmative cold ask still fails while documented prohibitions pass. Four more fixtures. Sixth round closed the standing-program gaps: the paywall cadence now requires current activity (an active row, a completed experiment started within eight weeks, or a planned row dated within 60 days) so one historical test cannot satisfy the gate forever; the push prime and the App Review popup may not share a step (the after-first-value slot goes to one prompt, the other waits for the next natural moment); and the push not-applicable exemption requires a substantive reason, not a bare label. The fixture harness gained a forbiddenText assertion so current-activity fixtures can prove the backlog codes stay silent while other gates still fire. Six more fixtures. Seventh round: a live app's first dated planned experiment now satisfies the cadence (the empty branch counts planned rows inside the horizon), a dated loop-economics row must carry a numeric k in the k column before it reads as a measurement, review/push prompts are correlated by numbered step so separate rows sharing a step fail without the words 'same step', and 'push permission: not applicable' earns the exemption on the same reasoned terms as 'push notifications'. Four more fixtures. Eighth round: the shipped UGC band table's empty Budget/Entered cells no longer satisfy the scale model (an operative band record is required — a populated table row, or a numeric budget plus dated current-band entry in prose), overdue first-measurement commitments fail (due dates live in a current window, not just under the 60-day ceiling), the Email + push router row now routes push work to ONBOARDING.md/ANALYTICS.md/TECH_SPEC.md/POST_LAUNCH_OPS.md with check:onboarding and check:analytics-catalog gates, and the paywall LaunchBench scenario teaches the current-activity contract including the dated-planned alternative. Three more fixtures. Ninth round: backlog rows must define their experiment (substantive hypothesis, variant, and primary-metric cells, with a recorded result for completed rows — a date plus a status word satisfies nothing, and missing definition columns fail closed), the push/review step-collision check reuses the canonical review-term set (native review and rating prompt aliases correlate too), and the push-lifecycle scenario is marked behavioral because triggers, caps, and event-catalog coverage are graded behaviorally while check:onboarding deterministically covers the prime. Two more fixtures. Tenth round: named step labels correlate review/push rows the same way numbered ones do, illustrative k copy (example/benchmark/self-compounds) is excluded and a k line must carry a measured qualifier, date, or week reference, punctuation-filled band cells no longer read as evidence (budget needs its number, evidence needs a date or substance), and short standard metric identifiers like CVR/ARPU/LTV count as defined experiments. Four more fixtures. Eleventh round: a combined step row naming both prompts (App Review popup; push permission prime) is the collision itself unless an explicit next-moment ordering separates them, and whole-cell negative values (unknown, NA, not yet, none, dashes) no longer satisfy the experiment-definition or band-evidence checks — an empty state wearing characters defines nothing. Three more fixtures. Twelfth round: a measured k must arrive with its cycle time and trend (line path region-checked, row path column-checked, commitment alternative unchanged), only a modeled band's row counts as operative UGC evidence (a Notes row with a budget number enters no band), the push exemption is mutually exclusive with affirmative push instructions (declaring not-applicable then instructing a launch ask stands on the ask, which fails), and loop regions end at the next heading of the opening level so a ### section cannot annex the next ### section's tables. Four more fixtures. Thirteenth round: the paywall scenario joins the behavioral harness (its tooling and effort-diversion assertions are not validator-checkable), placement timing alone no longer passes the push gate (explicit soft-prime evidence required before the system dialog), completed paywall experiments must record cohort-economics evidence over a renewal window (a day-one conversion delta is not a decision), the loop trend must be an explicit value rather than the section's own guidance prose, negative measurement cells (not measured / no decision yet) record nothing, and a recorded creator-content exemption stands even when the shipped UGC template remains on disk. Five more fixtures. Fourteenth round: the system dialog must be user-initiated from the prime surface (an automatic delayed hard ask fails), the exemption line's own reason is inspected for smuggled asks, cohort evidence is polarity-checked (naming the noun while negating it is not evidence), and the cycle-time number must belong to the cycle-time phrase rather than a nearby k value. Four more fixtures. Fifteenth round: cohort evidence is judged clause-by-clause so availability negatives (renewal window unavailable) affirm nothing, a measured row's k must equal invites times conversion within rounding tolerance, loop measurements carry a recency contract (weekly window once the app has been live five weeks, 90-day absolute floor, dated rows required over week-one prose), and push-notification-priming wording is recognized as the canonical subject. Six more fixtures. Sixteenth round: the first-measurement commitment applies only before the loop is running (a long-live app cannot keep postponing), percentage conversion rates normalize before the k formula check, the UGC region must state the founder gate itself (the word budget authorizes nothing), a negated capability statement (cannot show native notifications) reads as exemption reason rather than ask, and an explicitly undecided prose decision records no trend. Five more fixtures. Seventeenth round: the recency date must sit on the k measurement line itself (unrelated dated notes re-arm nothing), the pre-dialog tap must be an affirmative choice (a dialog after tapping Decline fails), declarative dialog behavior (the system dialog opens on launch) conflicts with an exemption the same as an instruction, future-tense cohort plans with no number are not observed results, and the shares/activation header aliases feed the same k arithmetic. Five more fixtures. Eighteenth round: the exemption reason recognizes declarative flows (the dialog opens on launch) not just imperatives, an automatically opening dialog fails regardless of a later tap, completed experiments need downstream economics (trial-to-paid, churn, renewal window — trial starts alone are top-of-funnel), a prose k stating its own factors must satisfy the formula, goal lines cannot supply the cycle time and trend for a measured k, roster counts are read from their own table columns (budget digits size no roster), and the forbidden-only fixtures now also assert the validator's normal report so a crash cannot pass as acceptance. Six more fixtures.

Centralizes the founder cockpit's business-access labels in scripts/lib/founder-copy.ts, the repository's sole machine-state-to-founder-text boundary. The cockpit renderer and founder-operator validator now import that shared presentation function from the sanctioned module, while fixtures continue to pin Active, Ready, Needs your help, and access-pending output against independent literal expectations. This closes PR #65's required P1 review thread without weakening the regression that caught the original false-green.

Founder cockpit account cards now translate every valid operator, Doppler, and account-access state instead of silently falling back to 'Not set up yet' for active or ready businesses. The renderer maps active, ready, founder_action_needed, access_pending, and access_ready to distinct founder-readable labels.

Founder-operator fixtures now pin literal Active and Ready output independently of the shared translation helper. This closes the false-green where the renderer and validator reused the same incomplete mapping and agreed on an incorrect cockpit.

The motion acceptance contract stops being prose-only, closing the one PR #59 review thread (P1) that merge deliberately deferred: new gate check:motion-contract makes the contract undriftable. The spring-family bands stated in premium-mobile-craft.md's two-family table, their mirror in motion-craft-benchmarks.md, the token table's ms values, and the PremiumMotion preset bounces must all match design-system/tokens.json, PremiumCraft.swift, and the three experience-card canon files — a band that outlaws its own cited canon (the exact blocker the pre-PR review caught by hand) is now a build failure. durationCinematic is banned from the in-app craft doctrine outright, and every benchmarks line naming it must carry its web/brand routing. A symbolic spring response must resolve to a real numeric DesignTokens.Motion member or it errs — the enum ships no expressive member, which is why variable-reward-card.md states the numeric 0.5 response; damping is always range-checked. Eighteen fixtures pin the gate both ways across nine review rounds (shipped skill passes; band-mirror drift, token-value drift, canon-outside-band, preset-duration drift, lost or duplicated table rows, stripped bounce annotations, malformed token references, unresolvable symbolic spring responses, duplicated family rows, punctuated identifier references, malformed decimal literals, template-copy drift, Swift-value drift, duplicated mirror statements, inverted family ranges, Swift members deleted out from under the table, and cinematic-leak each fail), it joins the audit plan in both layouts, the LaunchBench allowlist, docs/VALIDATORS.md, and failure-cards.md (motion-contract-prose-only). The motion-craft-prose-never-applied behavioral scenario covers the half a static gate structurally cannot see: an agent citing the benchmark file while shipping default eases on earned moments, one-sided navigation transitions, no Reduce Motion fallbacks, and no Animation Hitches profile. Suite 416 green. Two Codex review rounds on the PR hardened the gate itself: the parsed preset duration member is compared against the table row's token (a preset silently moving from durationFast to durationBase now fails), the loose row count became the exact required six-token set, a preset cell that drops its (bounce N) annotation errs instead of skipping every check, and the identifier matchers consume full names so motion.durationReveal2 can no longer pass as durationReveal. The behavioral scenario's missing-press-states failure moved from should_say to the hard must_catch list, and its gate instruction names the skill package explicitly — check:motion-contract is not an app-repo script, so grading an app checkout on running it would fail by construction. A third review round closed the gate's last two self-blindnesses: a symbolic spring response must resolve to a real numeric DesignTokens.Motion member or it errs (the NaN-skip had certified a snippet that would not even compile — variable-reward-card.md's reveal spring now states the numeric 0.5 response the reconciliation note already defined, since the enum ships no expressive member), and a duplicated press/celebrate row in the family table errs instead of silently overwriting the earlier canon. The cards' wider brief/moderate/expressive prose vocabulary against the actual Swift enum members is pre-existing drift tracked as its own follow-up. A fourth round hardened the parsers themselves: token references capture to the closing backtick and PremiumMotion names include hyphens, so punctuated near-identifiers err as unknown instead of escaping or truncating to a valid prefix (the motion.* namespace label in the table header is the one explicit exemption); spring literals parse under a strict decimal grammar with a spring_malformed error whenever a .spring(response: site fails to parse, so 0..5 cannot slide through as NaN; and the failure card now sends the recovering agent to the skill repo for the gate command, matching the scenario fix. A fifth round (concurrent with #60 taking v0.34.0, so this release is v0.35.0) closed the binary-truth blind spots: the gate now validates the token artifacts that actually ship beside PremiumCraft.swift — templates/design-system/tokens.json and DesignTokens.swift must match their top-level counterparts (template_tokens.drift), a preset's resolved Swift duration value must equal the documented milliseconds (preset.value_drift — naming the right member was never enough if the member's value moved), the spring-family mirror must appear exactly once so a stale appended statement cannot coexist with the current canon (family_mirror.duplicate), and the behavioral scenario states the dropped gesture-velocity handoff in its prompt and grades it as a hard must_catch assertion. A sixth round finished the sweep: every numeric table row is compared against its Swift enum value independently of whether a PremiumMotion preset rides it (durationReveal, durationCinematic, and stagger were previously outside the comparison), an inverted family range errs because an empty valid range gates nothing, and the spring parser tolerates Swift whitespace after the opening parenthesis so a reformatted recipe cannot hide from the site counter. A seventh round closed the deletion case: a documented token whose numeric member is removed from the DesignTokens.Motion enum errs (token_row.swift_member_missing) instead of silently skipping the value comparison while the shipped Swift stops compiling. Concurrent merges kept re-versioning this release: #60 took 0.34.0 and #62 took 0.35.0, so the gate lands as v0.37.0 after #63 took 0.36.0. An eighth round swapped the token-reference membership test to Object.hasOwn so prototype names like motion.constructor cannot pass as shipped tokens, and corrected this note's own stale symbolic-response sentence to describe the shipped behavior. A ninth round hardened the Swift-side parsers the same way the doc-side ones were: enum members parse under the strict decimal grammar and a Double whose literal does not parse errs as member_malformed (a non-compiling 0..5 can no longer register as NaN and skip the band check), and the PremiumMotion matcher captures fully qualified references so press.extra or press/extra cannot truncate to a valid preset name.

The in-app motion lane gets its swipe-file. New references/motion-craft-benchmarks.md carries ten named, numeric recipes (R1-R10) distilled from a full 300-post mine of the 60fps.design catalog plus frame-by-frame reads of its eight highest-engagement videos: asynchronous-grid liveness, two-phase celebration bloom, overshoot-and-settle object landing, pinch-open perspective accordion, scrub-linked theming, data-driven 3D extrusion with camera turn, motion-blur-as-velocity-cue, one-saturated-hero color discipline, contained edge-warp (explicitly web-lane only — the frame-read showed the exemplar is a website scroll effect), and the scratch-card reward reveal that maps directly onto the Variable Reward experience card. Every recipe states which motion token it rides (reconciling the tokens.json motion.* scale, the PremiumMotion.* SwiftUI presets, and the experience cards' brief/moderate/expressive vocabulary in one table), which experience card or craft detail it serves, and its catalog exemplars with engagement provenance — and every recipe is phrased as checkboxes a reviewer can verify on a screen recording, because the enforcement layer for generated UI code does not exist yet and adjectives do not gate. The catalog's engagement figures are labeled point-in-time and banned from founder/marketing copy.

The spring vocabulary is centralized instead of scattered. premium-mobile-craft.md section 1 now carries the two-family numeric canon the 2026-07-26 audit found hiding inside three experience cards: press springs (response 0.3-0.4, dampingFraction 0.7-0.8, no visible overshoot — a control responding) versus celebrate springs (response 0.45-0.5, dampingFraction 0.5-0.7 — an object landing), citing peak-end-card.md (0.45/0.7), mastery-and-status-card.md (0.5/0.7), and variable-reward-card.md (0.6) as the existing canon rather than inventing a parallel vocabulary. The celebrate band is explicit about its two ends: 0.6-0.7 gives the one soft settle right for sheet-level reveals (where the card canon sits), 0.5-0.6 is reserved for earned objects that should visibly oscillate 1-2 times, below 0.5 reads as a toy. The independent pre-PR review caught the first cut stating the family as 0.5-0.6 flat — a checklist that would have failed two of the three cards it cited as canon — and caught the table implying PremiumMotion.press shares the response/damping parameterization when it actually expresses the same physics through .spring(duration:bounce:); both are stated honestly now. A Motion.celebrate token promotion is named as a deliberate non-goal — doing it right means theme.tokens.json + PremiumCraft.swift + check:token-promotion in one change.

Two missing pattern families join the craft doctrine. Shared-Element Continuity (matchedGeometryEffect / navigationTransition(.zoom) on iOS 18+, react-navigation shared elements, Flutter Hero) lands in premium-mobile-craft.md with the one-traveler-per-transition rule, the text-morph trap, and a mandatory Reduce Motion cross-fade fallback — the repo previously had zero hits for any shared-element API. Gesture & Scroll Physics lands in motion-craft-benchmarks.md as numbers: the two-clocks rule (finger owns the clock at 1:1, tokens govern only the release), velocity handoff into every settle spring, rubber-band overscroll at the platform's ~0.55 resistance, pull-to-refresh arming at 60-80pt by distance with a single haptic, drag-to-dismiss committing on ~1,000pt/s projected velocity or 1/3 displacement with a no-overshoot spring-back, and full interruptibility.

The frame budget becomes doctrine. premium-mobile-craft.md now states the mechanical bar the account's own name implies: 16.6ms per frame (8.3ms on ProMotion), animate compositor-safe properties only (transform/opacity), never animate layout in scrolling contexts, blur/shadows called out as the expensive outliers, and profile with Instruments' Animation Hitches template on the oldest supported device before ship — with a zero hitch budget for press feedback and scrolling. The acceptance checklist and common failures grow matching rows so the craft audit asks about spring families, continuity, and hitches alongside the original five details. Provenance is layered honestly after the review pass: recipe numbers are frame-read measurements (±1 frame-interval), a few thresholds are labeled operationalizations of qualitative cues (R1's adjacency window, R2's contraction and clone stagger), and the gesture-physics constants are labeled platform-behavior defaults the catalog motivates but did not measure.

The source is registered, the wiring avoids the frozen entrypoint. source-registry.yaml gains x-com-60fpsdesign-catalog as an inspiration_benchmark (30-day cadence, the motionsites-ai precedent — its mobile counterpart), design-visual-system.md gains the Source Tooling line and routes step 6a to the recipe layer, quality-lens.md gains the Inspiration Sources bullet, and premium-mobile-craft.md gains the routing line under Platform Routing. SKILL.md is untouched: it sits at 46,077 of 46,080 budget bytes, so the new reference is reachable through the design and craft references it extends, exactly as the freeze-and-subtract discipline demands.

PR-review round (Codex) hardened five spots before merge: the cards' overloaded expressive name is reconciled explicitly (a 0.45-0.5s spring response and a ~500ms/durationReveal-bounded choreography duration are different quantities, not a contradiction); R1's in-app ambient variant paces on 1-2x durationReveal so the cinematic 1200ms token stays web/brand-lane as the table says; the SwiftUI shared-element bullet now states that matchedGeometryEffect does not bridge NavigationStack destinations and that the iOS 18 zoom transition needs .matchedTransitionSource on the source AND .navigationTransition(.zoom) on the destination; the velocity handoff names the real SwiftUI mechanism (DragGesture.Value.velocity into .interpolatingSpring initialVelocity — a projected end target alone carries no velocity); and landing-motion-craft.md links back to R9/R1 so the landing lane can discover its two web-lane recipes. The validator/LaunchBench ask for the new acceptance contract stays deliberately deferred with G8: a grep for spring numbers in generated app code is the words-not-work trap, and the honest gate needs a reality-probe design of its own.

The evidence bar is right-sized to consumer-app norms and essentials becomes the recommended first-launch scope. The 2026-07-26 audit's process finding, confirmed by the founder's own override on a real launch: the default full-scope apparatus burned two months producing governance artifacts and zero customer proof before being retired by hand, and most attempted launches died in planning with nobody deciding to stop. launch-phases.md's Launch Scopes now recommends essentials for a first launch (full is a deliberate flagship choice, never a default), renames the legacy lite value in place, and points at two new companion contracts.

founder-zero-operator.md gains The Consumer-Norm Evidence Bar: consumer-app research is store and competitor data, review mining, social language, keyword demand, and a live funnel — never invented research governance. Formative-interview programs behind privacy reviewers, external encrypted data planes, compensation approvals, and role-separated dry runs are escalated only for a hard constraint (medical/health claims, minors, regulated categories), at the minimum that satisfies it, as a founder decision with the cost stated.

project-state.md gains The Pre-Build Clock: project.kickoff_date is recorded when orient completes, and validate:launch-state errors on an invalid or future date and warns (project.pre_build_stall) when a launch is still in phases 0-2 more than 45 days after kickoff. The response is a founder decision, not silence — cut scope to essentials, re-run Go/Pivot/Kill, or record the deliberate dated choice to continue. Most launches that die do so in planning, quietly; the clock makes the quiet visible. Three fixtures, the evidence-bar-overengineered LaunchBench scenario, and stable-section compressions keep launch-phases.md inside its 64KiB budget and SKILL.md inside 46,080 bytes. Review round made the default real end to end: templates/PROJECT_STATE.yaml now seeds launch_scope: essentials (project-state.md's guidance matches — full is a deliberate flagship choice, not the generated state's default), a blank kickoff_date past orientation is an error rather than a silently disarmed clock, and the flagship launch-tier-overproduction behavioral scenario is rewritten to the scope/essentials contract so graded responses are no longer measured against the retired full/lite vocabulary. One more fixture.

Founder gates come back. The 2026-07-26 audit's ground-truth finding: a real launch carried a fully worked $200/day paid-UA plan while lanes.paid_user_acquisition sat at deferred behind blockers: ["founder-gated: paid campaign launch and budget spend"] for eight weeks — the founder never declined; the question was simply never asked again, because blocker strings were exempt from the dated/staleness bar every reason field already faces. A founder gate is a pause awaiting a decision, not a termination.

check:lane-coverage now scans founder-gated blockers on partial/blocked/deferred lanes: they carry the real, non-future ISO date they were last presented (an undated, typo'd, or forward-dated gate is one nobody can ever call stale — warning pre-launch, error on a live phase_6 app), and past the 30-day re-engagement window the agent must re-present the gate with what changed and re-date it with the founder's response (founder_gate_reengagement_due — warning pre-launch, error once live, because a live app with its growth levers parked behind a forgotten question is the distribution-never-turns-on failure mode). Review round: the presentation date reads only from the documented slot — between the gate keyword and the colon — so a campaign or deadline date later in the free text can neither keep a stale gate looking fresh nor age a fresh one, and the LaunchBench scenario's guidance now matches the validator (undated gates on a live app are a failing check, not a warning). One more fixture. Second round: active gates are matched by the canonical prefix syntax only (a blocker starting founder-gated/founder-only/awaiting founder) — the shipped template's standing policy note ('Founder approval is required before paid spend') is a reminder, not a presented decision, and never ages into a false stale-gate error. One more fixture. Third round: project-state.md's policy text now matches the validator (undated AND stale gates are errors on a live app, warnings pre-launch), docs/VALIDATORS.md's check:lane-coverage entry names the founder-gate enforcement, and the forward-date rejection carries one day of tolerance so a founder east of UTC recording today's local date is same-day, not forward-dated. One more fixture.

The contract ships as procedure, not just gate: project-state.md gains the Founder-Gate Re-Engagement section (re-dating happens only when the gate is actually re-presented; silence defers again and never converts to approval, and never means forever), founder-zero-operator.md's Conversation Protocol gains the re-engagement lifecycle step, the post-launch Weekly Ops Review's growth step lists gates older than 30 days, and the spend founder-gate carries the 30-day comeback. Five fixtures and the founder-gate-deferred-forever LaunchBench scenario pin both directions.

The pre-build kill gate exists. The 2026-07-26 fresh-eyes audit's most corroborated finding: the skill had no mechanism anywhere in Phases 0-5c that could stop a mediocre idea before design, build, store, revenue, and legal effort was spent on it — the only Kill verdict in the system fired at day-30/day-90, after the app had shipped. Phase 1 now ends at a Go, Pivot, Or Kill checkpoint that mirrors the post-launch Kill-Or-Scale Review's rigor: the agent assembles the evidence (category revenue reality, wedge, demand signal), the founder decides, and a Kill here is the process working — it costs a research doc instead of a shipped app.

Category Revenue Reality turns AppKittie data collection into a judged gate: RESEARCH.md carries top-competitor revenue rows with sources, a stated bar (default: top 10 gross $5M/yr combined with two independent apps clearing $1M each), and an explicit pass/fail. check:research at done parses the revenue and source columns (a dollar amount drifting in an unrelated cell, or a blank/undated source, is not a sourced estimate) and requires the judgment line — collecting the numbers was never the gate, the judged number is.

The verdict is enforced at substance level: check:research requires a completed Go, Pivot, Or Kill row (ISO date, evidence cells, verdict, named decision-maker — an agent recording Go for itself is the exact bypass the founder-only gate exists to stop), fails placeholder evidence, refuses a done lane whose latest verdict is not Go, and requires the lanes.research.go_pivot_kill_decision/decided_at state mirror to match the doc's verdict AND date. Since every lane depends on research, Phase 2 design work cannot legitimately start over a missing or non-Go verdict. Ten fixtures and the pre-build-kill-gate-skipped LaunchBench scenario pin the gate in both directions. Second review round: a prose mention of either section no longer skips its checks (the gate reads the parsed heading, not the phrase), the verdict table must keep its evidence columns (Date | Verdict | Decided by alone is a decision with the reasons removed), and the stated bar must be a substantive number before a pass/fail judgment counts. Three more fixtures. Third round hardened the founder-only and phase boundaries: the verdict is enforced from phase_2 onward even while the research lane is still partial (advancing to design without the checkpoint is the bypass, not a shortcut), and the Decided-by cell must name the founder — automation identities (agent, Claude, Codex, bot) are rejected, because an agent recording Go for itself is the exact miss the gate exists to stop. Two more fixtures. Fourth round closed the remaining routes: at phase_2+ a deferred/not_needed research lane no longer suppresses the missing-artifact error (deferring research out of existence is not a route around the checkpoint); same-day follow-up verdicts supersede earlier rows (later table rows win date ties); the founder counts by recorded name (project.owner) as well as role, so 'Daisy Rivera' passes while automation identities still fail; and the three evidence columns are matched by name, so a table renamed to Notes/Opinion/Summary fails rather than passing on cell count. Four more fixtures. Fifth round: the gate also fires the moment any downstream lane (experience, product, design, content assets, engineering) goes active regardless of recorded phase; malformed decision rows (mistyped date, missing verdict keyword) are reported instead of silently losing to an older verdict; the decision-maker reads from the named Decided-by column, never positionally; and column lookups match the table's header row only, so data cells containing header keywords satisfy nothing. Four more fixtures; the research gate ends the slice at header-scoped, name-scoped, phase-independent enforcement.

The numbers loop closes: a live app is measured in dollars and users, not deploy logs. The 2026-07-26 fresh-eyes audit found the failure in table form on real launches — a post-launch evidence file recording verified deploys and COMPLETE uploads with zero user or revenue numbers, a day-30 retro sixteen days overdue with every cell reading 'unverified — confirm in RevenueCat', and a portfolio-wide grep finding no MRR/DAU number in any business state. Machinery proof passed every gate; reality was never read.

lanes.post_launch_ops.live_since is the new clock: the first approved-for-sale date, recorded once. From it check:post-launch derives the retro due dates (launch +7/+30/+90, one week grace) and fails a day-30/day-90 checkpoint still uncompleted past due — the dodge the existing verdict gates could not see, since every one of them fired only after a completion date was recorded. Never completing the checkpoint was the one move that kept the zombie app green.

The Weekly Ops Review now opens with the live pull and proves it in the log: once an app is live past two weeks, the weekly log needs dated rows, the latest at most two weeks old, with real numbers in the crash-free/retention cells. 'unverified', 'TBD', and adjectives fail (post_launch_ops.weekly_numbers_missing, weekly_log_stale, weekly_log_missing), and the same placeholder scan now applies to kill-or-scale evidence cells (kill_or_scale_evidence_placeholder) — non-empty was never the bar, the number was. A recorded Kill verdict exempts a wound-down app, so the one legitimate quiet state stays clean. Ships the metrics-theater anti-pattern, the post-launch-metrics-never-operated LaunchBench scenario, and ten fixtures covering the new gates in both directions; ten fixtures land across the new gates.

Review hardening on the same slice (three Codex threads, all confirmed): live-phase severity — a phase_6/phase_6b project can no longer dodge the numbers gates by leaving the lane partial (severity derives from the phase, not only lane done, with a phase-vanish fixture pinning the real-world shape); the Kill exemption must be earned, not typed — kill_or_scale_decision alone no longer silences the gates, the state mirror must be complete and a completed retro checkpoint must actually carry a Kill verdict; and live_since is validated as a real past calendar date (round-tripped, not in the future), so a typo'd month or forward-dated launch cannot disarm the clock via NaN math. Three more fixtures; test:validators 395 -> 399. Second review round tightened the same edges: the Kill exemption additionally requires the checkpoint to be completed in the Retro Window with a valid past date and a filled non-placeholder evidence pack (Kill typed into the verdict table alone no longer exempts); checkpoint completion itself requires a valid non-future calendar date (TBD in the Date cell is not completion); weekly-log row dates get the same strict validation so a future or impossible row cannot anchor freshness; and metric cells must hold a measured value — a percentage or the dated-blocker form — not incidental digits inside adjectives. Four more fixtures; test:validators 399 -> 403. Third round closed the last two seams: the retro verdict-substance checks (verdict filled, evidence pack complete, state mirror agreeing) now run for live phases too, so a phase_6 project with the lane still partial cannot record a checkpoint date over an empty verdict row; and the weekly gate enforces the runbook's own money contract — the Notes cell needs MRR as a dollar figure (MRR $0 counts) or a dated blocker, because a metrics review that never touches money is metrics theater with extra steps. Two more fixtures pin the third round. Fourth round made measurement column-appropriate end to end: the Kill exemption and the verdict substance bar both require the MRR-trend cell to carry a dollar amount and the retention cell a percentage (kill_or_scale_evidence_unmeasured — 'flat' and 'declining' are directions, not measurements), and the weekly Notes cell must carry an MRR-labeled amount with a digit, so 'ad spend $500' and 'MRR $...' no longer pass as revenue. Two more fixtures; 408 green. Fifth round anchored every remaining date to the launch: checkpoint completion counts only inside the launch-anchored window (on or after live_since plus due-day-minus-grace, so a recycled pre-launch date suppresses nothing), dated blockers validate their embedded calendar date ('blocked: ... 2026-99-99' is a placeholder in disguise), and all four verdict evidence columns are typed — founder hours needs a number and unit economics a number or an explained n/a. Three more fixtures; the slice ends at 411 green.

The portfolio board renders. render-business-control-plane-workspace.ts gains an aggregate mode: repeated --business <dir> flags each name a business workspace (state/business.json + PROJECT_STATE.yaml), and the renderer concatenates one entry per business into the businesses[] array the workspace schema and the prototype board page already modeled — the same per-business adapter, run N times, one board out. Two businesses resolving to the same slug fail loudly (business_workspace.duplicate_business_id) instead of silently overlaying rows, --check verifies a committed board exactly as it does single-business output, and single-root mode is byte-for-byte unchanged. control-plane.md's Portfolio Layer section documents the command; fixtures cover the two-business render, the check pass, and the slug collision. With PORTFOLIO_REGISTRY.md as the decision surface and this as the rendered read model, the second-launch founder has both halves of the portfolio layer.

Milestone celebrations now reach the founder. celebrationBeats/celebrationFor shipped in v0.25.0 and were verified present by check:founder-copy — but nothing ever rendered or spoke them: the dictionary carried eight progress beats while the renderer never imported the function, the words-not-work trap applied to the skill's own warmth. The cockpit now computes the latest earned-but-unspoken beat from phaseOrder and shows it as a 'Worth a moment' card until narrative.last_celebrated_phase records it as spoken; project-state.md carries the say-then-record loop (say the beat in the reply, then set the field, never the reverse); and check:founder-copy fails when the renderer loses the wiring (founder_copy.celebration_unwired), so the beats can never go silently decorative again.

check:founder-copy gains its first fixtures — the gate that proves every other founder surface could fail had nothing proving it could fail itself. Four cases: the shipped skill passes, raw snake_case on a founder surface fails, a renderer without celebration wiring fails, and empty narrative past orient fails. That last one makes the PROJECT_STATE template comment true: it has claimed since v0.25.0 that check:founder-copy fails on empty or placeholder narrative once the project is past orient, and until now no such check existed — the promise is enforced (founder_copy.narrative_stale.*) with the shipped template exempt through its own orient phase.

Money-lane depth pass from the 2026-07-26 audit backlog: the three revenue lanes were rich in benchmarks and thin in procedures — rules an agent could quote but not evaluate. Five fills turn them into numbers and steps.

Paid-UA stop/scale rules now evaluate against four recorded Decision Thresholds in growth/PAID_UA.md: attribution tolerance (default ±20% across RevenueCat / store console / PostHog / self-reported), payback window (default 90 days against realized LTV), creative signal floor (default 2x target CPA or 7 days per creative before judging it), and scale trigger (default 14 consecutive days at or under target CPA at approved spend). check:paid-ua requires all four labels, the template carries them, and the 'documented tolerance' that was never documented now has a home and a default. Review caught the label-only gap in the first cut: a done lane now also needs an actual number per threshold (comments stripped first, so the template's commented defaults cannot stand in), with a valueless-thresholds fixture pinning it.

revenue-monetization.md gains §7a Price-Point Decision Procedure: anchor against 5-10 competitors (AppKittie IAP data plus live listings) with a real anchor table, choose two or three candidates biased high per the §10 benchmarks, design the trial against the value moment via onboarding-conversion.md, record the decision with the founder's dated approval, and revisit on evidence (cancellation mix, realized LTV, kill-or-scale pack) through change-cascade.md. check:revenue enforces the floor at done: pricing decision section present, at least one real (non-example) competitor anchor row, and a dated founder approval — and its product-row count is now scoped to the Store Product ID table so anchor/cancellation/snapshot rows cannot stand in for a real product.

The nine billing-lifecycle and reactivation events §8a/§8b prescribe (billing_issue_detected through reactivated) existed only in reference prose — none were in the ANALYTICS.md Event Contract, and check:analytics-catalog never scanned revenue docs. The catalog now carries all nine plus cancellation_reason_selected, and REVENUE_OPS.md joins the reconciled surface docs so a revenue doc naming an uncataloged event fails like any other surface.

§8b gains cancellation-reason capture: a fixed six-code taxonomy asked at the in-app cancellation/pause moment (never a delayed email, never blocking the cancel), emitted as cancellation_reason_selected, aggregated into REVENUE_OPS.md's Cancellation-Reason Mix, and fed into the §7a pricing revisit, win-back targeting, and the kill-or-scale evidence pack. The template names the event as an extractable whole-line bullet (review caught it hiding in an HTML comment where the catalog reconciliation could not see it), so renaming or dropping it from ANALYTICS.md fails the cross-doc gate. A second review round finished the job: all nine lifecycle events are extractable bullets in REVENUE_OPS.md's Billing And Reactivation Events list, revenue-doc drift is an error whenever the REVENUE lane is done (not only when analytics is), and the pricing-approval check strips HTML comments first so a date typed inside the template's comment cannot pass as a founder approval.

tool-recipes/revenue-email-analytics.md gains the RevenueCat Economics Pull recipe: before every kill-or-scale checkpoint, pull MRR, realized LTV, download-to-paid, and the voluntary/involuntary churn split (docs basis recorded per the freshness rules), land them in REVENUE_OPS.md's new Economics Snapshot table, and route the consequences into the paid-UA thresholds, the pricing revisit, and the founder narration contract — the offering probe proves the plumbing, this reads what flows through it.

Wealth-path pass from the 2026-07-26 end-to-end audit: the skill was strong from idea to launch and silent from launch to portfolio. Every stop/scale rule gated one layer down (a paid channel, a creative format, a release) and nothing ever gated the app itself, so the tooling's default outcome was running the Weekly Ops Review on a plateaued app forever. Three fills: a whole-app Kill-Or-Scale Review, a portfolio layer for the second launch onward, and a founder-narration contract so progress is told, not just rendered.

post-launch-operations.md gains §9 Kill-Or-Scale Review, run at the day-30/day-90 retro checkpoints: the agent assembles an evidence pack from sources the rhythm already reads (MRR trend, D7/D30 cohort trend, CAC:LTV or payback, founder hours per week) and presents four verdict bands — Scale, Hold, Fix, Kill — with the verdict itself always the founder's call. The RevenueCat 2026 milestone statistics (only ~4.6% of new apps reach $10K/month; ~75% never clear the $1K-to-$10K climb) turn from motivational framing into the reason the question is mandatory. A Kill verdict is a wind-down with obligations (subscriber handling, store-rule refunds, data-deletion deadlines, a final retro that seeds the next launch), never an abandonment. LAUNCH_RETRO.md carries the verdict table, PROJECT_STATE.yaml records the decision and date, and check:post-launch enforces the substance rather than the heading: the verdict section must exist, and once the Retro Window records a completed Day 30/Day 90 pass that checkpoint's row must carry a real verdict with the state mirror holding a valid decision and ISO date (review caught the heading-only first cut — the exact zombie-app bypass the section warns about). The zombie-app failure card plus a LaunchBench scenario pin the miss.

The portfolio layer gives the repeat founder a board: templates/PORTFOLIO_REGISTRY.md (per-business stage/MRR/verdict/hours rows, an allocation paragraph, a cross-app learnings table fed by each retro, and the next-launch pipeline that makes killing an app feel like progress), routed from control-plane.md's new Portfolio Layer section and the post-launch lane row. New gate check:portfolio-registry is a no-op until the registry exists and structural once it does; it joins both package roots, the audit plan, the launchbench allowlist, and docs/VALIDATORS.md. Brand vocabulary, tokens, domains, and credentials still never move between businesses — learnings, engineering patterns, and founder-owned audiences do.

The founder-narration contract closes the delivery gap the 2026-07-25 audit named and left open: every cockpit instruction in the skill was a write-only verb (render, re-render, reconcile), and nothing anywhere told the agent to say anything to the founder. The Autopilot Run Contract now requires the narrative in the reply whenever the cockpit changes or a session ends — what happened, what is next, what needs the founder — with matching guidance in project-state.md and founder-zero-operator.md, and a behavioral LaunchBench scenario (cockpit-rendered-but-never-narrated) for the failure a static validator structurally cannot see. SKILL.md paid for the new clause under freeze-and-subtract: the runtime-split ground rule collapsed to a pointer at its own section and the versioning bullet lost its duplicate clause (46,078 of 46,080 bytes).

launch-coverage.md's Post-launch loop row and launch-phases.md Phase 6b acceptance now name the verdict and the registry, so the coverage audit catches a launch that runs the rhythm but never asks the question.

Review hardening on the same slice: the Post-launch operations routing row now loads control-plane.md for the second-business trigger and names PORTFOLIO_REGISTRY.md plus check:portfolio-registry in its outputs (an agent following the router alone could previously miss the portfolio contract entirely), and check:portfolio-registry rejects a blank board — the shipped template stays inert through its _example:_ row, but a registry whose Businesses table lists nothing real fails instead of passing on heading presence. SKILL.md paid for the routing addition with further freeze-and-subtract trims. Two more review rounds tightened the verdict contract to its full shape: a completed checkpoint's verdict now also needs every evidence cell filled (a verdict without the MRR/retention/economics/hours pack is a mood, not a decision), and the state mirror must agree with the latest completed checkpoint's verdict so a retro saying Kill can never coexist with state saying scale. Final round: the section check matches the real heading rather than a prose mention of the phrase, control-plane.md tells agents to run the portfolio gate against the founder workspace (bare from an app repo it no-ops by design) while naming one-row-per-business completeness as the founder's read rather than a machine check, and the Phase 6b acceptance line qualifies the verdict requirement by completed checkpoints so done-at-launch+7 stays satisfiable.

Gate-integrity pass from the 2026-07-26 end-to-end audit (15-agent workflow, every finding adversarially verified before landing). Five confirmed defects in the enforcement layer itself: two validator bypasses, one dead-by-construction gate, one structurally blocked eval lane, and a maintenance CI job that had failed every scheduled run since May without anyone noticing.

check:no-slop now reads HTML surfaces as HTML. proseOnly() stripped backtick spans on every surface, but a backtick has no syntax meaning in rendered HTML — a banned marketing word wrapped in backticks on launch-cockpit.html, onboarding.html, or design-room.html was invisible to the gate and fully visible to the founder. HTML surfaces route through a proseFromHtml() extractor that drops <code>/<pre>/tags and keeps backtick characters in scope; markdown keeps the code-span exemption. Two fixtures pin the asymmetry in both directions.

check:lane-coverage's dependency_override now has to earn the downgrade. Any single non-empty string ('not needed') converted the dependency_unlocked error into a warning — the quality bar existed but only ever warned, which is the words-not-work bypass in one field. The override must now pass the same dated/substantive reason bar as every other reason before the error downgrades; an undated or trivial override leaves the error standing and is itself flagged. A stale dated override still downgrades (drift to revisit, not proof the lanes were never independent) and its staleness warning rides along. Fixtures updated to pin the refusal and the stale path.

run-launchbench.ts's knownValidators allowlist had drifted from the real audit pipeline: check-revenue, check-no-slop, check-change-cascade, check-founder-copy, and check-template-safety are all PR-blocking gates that no LaunchBench scenario could legally cite — the Monetization lane's actual enforcement had zero scenario coverage by construction. The five entries are added, both RevenueCat scenarios now cite check-revenue alongside validate-project-state, and check:package-parity gained a structural cross-check that fails when a wired check/validate script is missing from the allowlist or an allowlist entry has no backing script, so the drift cannot recur silently.

check:revenue's MISSING_METADATA and product-type gates now judge table data rows, not the whole document. The resolved-pattern regex matched the shipped template's own column header ('MISSING_METADATA cleared?'), so the MISSING_METADATA error could never fire on any repo built from the template — a dead gate wearing a green check. The product-type check had the inverse bug: it matched the guidance sentence naming non_renewing_subscription, so it false-fired on every done revenue lane keeping template prose. Both are row-scoped now, with three new fixtures covering the traps failure-cards.md already documented: unresolved MISSING_METADATA, a lifetime SKU typed non_renewing_subscription, and a proof note missing Release-build confirmation. Review found the residual hole in the row-scope: a row answering plain 'no' in the 'MISSING_METADATA cleared?' column never repeats the MISSING_METADATA string, so the literal row check could not see it — the gate now also parses the clearance column itself and fails on a negative or unanswered cell, with a fourth fixture pinning exactly that row shape.

Repairs the weekly source-freshness refresh, which had failed all seven scheduled runs since 2026-06-08 — the drift-detection lane for fast-moving provider docs was silently inert. Root cause: the refresh renders docs/source-freshness/source-refresh.html with HTML-escaped URLs (&), and check:source-registry re-scanned that generated artifact and flagged its own output as unregistered sources. The generated HTML report joins the snapshot and report files in the scan exclusion, a fixture pins the regression, and the workflow's artifact-upload and PR steps run on failure too, so a future red refresh lands as a visible red PR instead of vanishing into a run log.

Revives the two conversion-craft references that were written in May, reviewed, and then never merged. feat/conversion-craft-marketingskills landed most of its work on main through later PRs (check-launch-narrative.ts, check-localization-research.ts, LAUNCH_NARRATIVE.md, localization-market-research.md), but references/conversion-copy.md and references/cro-landing.md fell off the branch and stayed there for two months. Every cross-reference in both files still resolves against current main, so they were merged as written rather than rewritten.

Wires the two references into the skill rather than dropping them in as orphans. Lane Routing gains a Landing CRO row and a Conversion copy row so an agent can actually reach them, and the split between them is explicit: cro-landing.md owns page structure where onboarding-conversion.md owns the in-app flow, and conversion-copy.md owns the words where cro-landing.md owns the layout. source-registry.yaml gains three entries the files depend on: the MIT-licensed marketingskills pack they are adapted from, the Google Play listing metadata policy, and the Core Web Vitals thresholds.

Bumps the dev-dependency group across both package roots at once: @anthropic-ai/sdk 0.104.1 to 0.115.0, @types/node ^22 to ^26, @vitejs/plugin-react ^4 to ^6, typescript ^5.7 to ^7.0, vite ^6.4 to ^8.1, plus motion, prettier, react, react-dom, tsx, and @types/react. Dependabot split this one group into two PRs by directory (#45 root, #46 runtime), and check:package-parity requires root and runtime devDependency versions to match exactly, so each PR broke parity on its own. #45 failed its audit for that reason and #46 was only green because its check ran against an older base. Landing both halves together is the only ordering that keeps main green.

Reformats scripts/lib/founder-copy.ts under prettier 3.9.6, which collapses the FounderPhase union onto one line now that it fits the print width. Formatting only, no behavior change. TypeScript 7.0.2, Vite 8.1.5, and @types/node 26.1.1 were verified locally against the full gate before this landed: tsc passes and all 353 validator fixtures pass, so the major bumps carry no source changes.

Teaches the check:no-slop banned-word matcher every regular inflection of a banned word. The matcher's trailing boundary excluded letters, so "leverage" failed the gate while "leverages", "leveraging", "utilized", "empowering", "streamlined", and "elevates" all walked through it. That is the words-not-work trap in miniature: the rule was real, the enforcement covered one spelling of it. The matcher now generates forms for the five regular suffixes (s, es, ed, d, ing) plus the two stem rules English needs, an e-final verb dropping its e before -ing ("leveraging") and a consonant-plus-y term pluralising as -ies ("tapestries").

Bounds the new tolerance at the regular inflections so a word that merely begins with a banned word keeps its own meaning: "elevator", "robustness", "utilization", and "embarkation" stay clean. Every form the current banned list generates was checked against the 235k-headword system dictionary, and the only real words it produces are inflections of their own base word. Six validator fixtures pin both halves, one per suffix rule plus a near-miss file that must stay silent, and all five positive fixtures go red against the old matcher.

Rewrites the six inflected banned words the sharper matcher found in references/, all of them warning-level guidance prose: "fosters dependency" becomes "encourages dependency", three "Elevates from 5-star" mappings become "Moves from 5-star", and the remaining "elevates" become "strengthens" and "raises". No shipped template needed a change, so the error-severity surfaces were already clean.

Rewrites the public front door against a benchmark of top AI/agent repos. README drops from ~300 lines to ~140: Quickstart moves above the fold (it sat at line 216 of 302, behind a 47-command wall), the What It Produces table goes from 24 paragraph-length cells to 10 one-clause rows, and Non-Negotiables goes from 18 dense bullets to 6, pointing at SKILL.md for the rest. The full validator reference moves to docs/VALIDATORS.md rather than being deleted.

Extends check:no-slop to this repo own public docs through a new --repo-root flag: README.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, SECURITY.md, and CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md error; AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md warn like references do. README claimed references/no-slop-writing.md governs every word this skill writes while the gate never scanned it, which is the words-not-work trap the founder-surface audit already named. The gate now reaches its own front door.

Adds the community-health surfaces the repo was missing: CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md, a root SECURITY.md scoped to this repo validators, workflows, and dependency chain (distinct from the shipped templates/SECURITY.md release plan), .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE bug and proposal forms plus config.yml, .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md mirroring the CONTRIBUTING gates, and .github/dependabot.yml covering both npm roots and the SHA-pinned actions.

Adds the missing translation boundary between machine state and the founder. render-launch-cockpit.ts printed raw PROJECT_STATE.yaml keys into HTML, so a founder read rows like "paid_tool_routing | not_started" on their own business dashboard; only one file in the repo (scripts/lib/founder-gate-presentation.ts) ever turned state into a sentence before a human saw it. scripts/lib/founder-copy.ts is now the single sanctioned path from state to founder-visible text, covering all 22 areas, 6 status values, 20 phase codes, 6 autonomy modes, and the provider route values, plus a 9-milestone progress spine that replaces the 22-row flat table as the founder's home view.

Reshapes the cockpit around the founder instead of the state machine. The page now opens with a narrated update (Since last time / What I am doing now / What I need from you) fed by a new top-level `narrative` block in PROJECT_STATE.yaml, then what only you can decide, then progress, then blockers pulled up from every area. Multi-agent bookkeeping (orchestration, agent operations, per-area detail, service verification wording) moved behind one collapsed technical-details disclosure. Two heading renames were coordinated with the validators that split on them: check-founder-operator-bootstrap.ts and check-agent-operations.ts.

Stops the founder-facing copy from leaking implementation detail. "AskUserQuestion when available" was printed on the founder's dashboard and BUSINESS_ACCESS.md, and the founder_experience/agent_role settings, raw status enums, phase ids, and ledger file paths were rendered beside them. BUSINESS_ACCESS.md's "One Next Action" section went from a 17-field labeled form to a narrative ask while keeping every string check:founder-operator requires. check-founder-operator-bootstrap.ts now compares the translated access labels rather than the raw enums, so the check stays real and the page stays readable.

New gate check:founder-copy makes "no raw machine value reaches a founder" a build failure rather than a review nit. It proves every value in lib/launch-state.ts has founder copy (a new area cannot ship unlabeled), then scans launch-cockpit.html, BUSINESS_ACCESS.md, and the four other founder-facing HTML surfaces for snake_case, SCREAMING_SNAKE, and pipe-delimited serialized records. Text inside <code>, inside a <details> disclosure, or inside a mustache placeholder is exempt, because marking a value as an identifier is the honest way to show a secret name a founder must paste.

Installs the no-ai-slop writing rules (petergyang/no-ai-slop, MIT) across every surface this skill writes and every marketing surface it generates. references/no-slop-writing.md carries the full banned-word, empty-adverb, empty-phrase, and named-pattern lists plus channel-specific limits for store metadata, ad headlines, email subject lines, and launch posts. Nine copy-producing lanes now load it before drafting. New gate check:no-slop parses its rule table out of that reference rather than duplicating it, so the doc an agent reads and the gate that fails the build cannot drift; it errors on 14 shipped copy surfaces and warns on guidance prose.

Adds eight progress beats tied to real phase exits. Every audit of the founder conversation found zero progress-acknowledgment language anywhere: the agent moved from a passing live-purchase test straight to the next requirement without ever telling the founder something good had happened. Beats are earned by a named condition (a validated sandbox and production purchase, a device run with evidence, store approval) and check:founder-copy fails when one is missing.

Renames launch_tier to launch_scope because "tier" collided with the founder's own app pricing tiers. Both keys and both value sets stay valid on read and "lite" resolves to "essentials", so a business repo launched before this rename keeps validating instead of silently failing its state file to gain a nicer word. Also fixes two rendering bugs found during the audit: proof.commands shipped one all-empty entry instead of an empty list, which defeated the cockpit's own fallback and rendered a blank unlabeled box, and tools.app_store_screenshots.selected_route was a pipe-delimited triple with a GitHub username baked into a single founder-visible cell.

Lifts the Change Cascade Map out of a markdown table and into data so it can be graded. change-cascade.md said a change to a launched app is not done until every impacted surface is "updated or explicitly marked unaffected", but the map lived in a human-readable table no validator could read — a cascade could silently skip App Preview, a localization, or the RevenueCat product name and still read as complete, which is the change-cascade-incomplete failure card by construction. references/cascade-edges.yaml now carries the same 10-surface inventory and 9 change types as data (each with a `mirrors` field naming the table row it comes from, so drift between the two is visible), and check:change-cascade grades the change_cascade block a launch run records in its own PROJECT_STATE.yaml.
